summary: The design fits the plan subsystem, but the current plan model and compiler only support one node shape, while execution-plan recovery and tool dispatch impose additional lifecycle, policy, and persistence contracts. The highest risks are schema discrimination, delegate resource ownership, side-effect enforcement, and rejection/recovery semantics.

suggestions.title: Make plan nodes a backward-compatible discriminated union
suggestions.rationale: `ExecutionPlan.nodes` is currently `List[PlanNode]`; `PlanNode` requires `tool` and forbids extra fields. The compiler also hardcodes every node as type `"tool"`, while the validator and repair code assume `PlanNode`. A `DelegatePlanNode` cannot work as a sibling model until parsing, compilation, validation, persistence, and repair all discriminate node kind explicitly. Preserve existing plans by defaulting the discriminator to `"tool"`.

suggestions.title: Reuse the existing dispatch and storage pipeline instead of duplicating it
suggestions.rationale: `PlanToolNode` already owns manager dispatch, retries, timeout handling, unknown-outcome refusal, task-memory receipts, fan-out, guards, and ArtifactRef storage. A separate delegate executor risks bypassing `_store` provenance retention or diverging from `ToolManager.execute_tool`. Extract a shared call/store service or override only proposal resolution while retaining the existing execution machinery.

suggestions.title: Specify delegate-pool ownership across fresh, resumed, and repaired flows
suggestions.rationale: `build_plan_flow` currently registers only `PlanToolNode` and supplies only the `"tool"` factory. `AgentsFlow` materializes fresh nodes per run, and both `plan_resume` and `plan_repair` rebuild flows through `build_plan_flow`. A live Needle pool must therefore be injected into every factory path, while `ProcessPoolExecutor` shutdown must be owned by the toolkit/application rather than an individual node.

suggestions.title: Build ToolSpec from the authoritative tool schema surface
suggestions.rationale: The proposed adapter assumes every manager entry has `args_schema`, but `ToolManager` also stores `ToolDefinition` entries with `input_schema`. `AbstractTool.get_schema()` already strips injected context fields and emits the framework's normalized parameter shape; raw `args_schema.model_json_schema()` would expose fields the delegate must not provide and may mishandle wrapped or untyped tools. Add one bounded adapter supporting both representations and preserve `$defs` correctly.

suggestions.title: Use one authoritative runtime argument-validation contract
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractTool.validate_args()` performs framework-specific coercion and validation, while `ToolManager.execute_tool()` applies permissions, credentials, result hooks, and failure normalization. Directly calling `args_schema.model_validate()` in the delegate can reject values the manager accepts or silently differ from its handling of context fields and extra keys. Add a pure validation helper that rejects malformed/unknown proposal arguments before dispatch, then pass the accepted arguments through the manager exactly once.

suggestions.title: Enforce side-effect policy from host configuration, not plan text
suggestions.rationale: `validate_plan()` currently receives only a plan and optional ToolManager; the existing allowlist is layered separately in `catalog.py`, and `ExecutionPlanToolkit` checks the effective allowlist during recovery. A plan-level `allow_side_effects: true` cannot establish that the agent configuration permits it. Inject an immutable delegate policy, intersect it with the existing allowlist, validate before execution, and re-check immediately before dispatch so mutable tool metadata cannot widen authority.

suggestions.title: Define rejection and escalation as persisted execution outcomes
suggestions.rationale: The current `ArtifactRef` has only `ok`, `skipped`, `partial`, and `error`; repair eligibility is based on `status="error"`, while partial fan-outs are explicitly not repairable. The proposed `on_reject="escalate"` therefore has no durable representation or clear path into bounded replanning, especially for per-item fan-out rejects. Add bounded structured rejection metadata and specify whether escalation becomes repair-eligible error data or an intentionally terminal status.

suggestions.title: Do not let confidence=None silently bypass a configured confidence gate
suggestions.rationale: If `min_confidence=0.8` is configured and a fine-tuned backend returns `None`, treating the gate as unavailable accepts an unscored proposal under the strongest-looking policy. Make unscored proposals an explicit policy choice, such as `reject_unscored` by default when a threshold is set, with `allow_unscored` or backend-agreement modes opt-in and validator-visible.

suggestions.title: Keep proposal traces bounded, redacted, and outside checkpoints by default
suggestions.rationale: Plan checkpointing deliberately projects only the plan-run envelope and excludes responses, while manifests and node errors are bounded to prevent payload leakage. Raw instructions, facts, and model arguments can contain secrets or high-cardinality fan-out data; appending them directly to a trace log would violate those existing safety properties. Use an opt-in external trace sink with size limits, redaction, retention controls, and hashes/metadata as the default persisted record.

suggestions.title: Separate backend implementations from the core contract and avoid an unnecessary llama-cpp dependency
suggestions.rationale: The core package currently uses optional extras and lazy imports for heavyweight integrations. A `llama-server --parallel` backend is an HTTP client and should use the repository's async HTTP conventions; it does not require the `llama-cpp-python` embedding package. Keep protocol/models in the plan package, put Needle behind a lazy optional extra with a top-level picklable process worker, and make pool shutdown idempotent.

suggestions.title: Add adversarial tests at the plan, recovery, and integration boundaries
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests explicitly protect manager dispatch, payload exclusion, fan-out concurrency, allowlists, and checkpoint projection. Extend those seams with accepted/rejected proposals, unknown tools, malformed and extra arguments, template/input limits, unscored confidence, side-effect denial, backend fallback, per-item escalation, cancellation, resume, repair, and idempotent registration. The tests should assert that rejected proposals never call `execute_tool` and that checkpointed runs retain no raw proposal payloads.

suggestions.title: Defer standalone AgentCrew support until its execution contract is adapted
suggestions.rationale: AgentCrew's `ToolNode` directly invokes `tool.execute()` and stores stringified results, whereas plan nodes dispatch through `ToolManager` and publish payload-free `ArtifactRef` values. Registering a delegate node in the flow registry does not make those contracts interchangeable. Keep the first implementation plan-scoped; add a separate Crew adapter only after permissions, working-memory semantics, and lifecycle ownership are defined.
